text:
Jo Brighton Skills Center enrolled 2 Asian students in 2024-25
Two Asian students were enrolled at Jo Brighton Skills Center in the 2024-25 school year, the same number as the previous year, according to the Michigan Department of Education.
Records show Jo Brighton Skills Center enrolled 192 students during the 2024-25 school year. Asian students made up 1% of the student body, the third least represented ethnicity. White students were the largest group, comprising 63% (121) of enrollment.
The school is in School District of the City of Wyandotte School District, which has a central office in Wyandotte.
Of the nine schools in School District of the City of Wyandotte School District, Roosevelt High School had the highest enrollment of Asian students in the 2024-25 school year.
Academic performance in Michigan remains below pre-pandemic levels. The 2024 NAEP results show the share of students reaching the basic benchmark in core subjects is about 10 percentage points lower than in 2019—except for fourth-grade math, which saw a decline of just 2 points.
Achievement gaps between ethnic groups also persist. On average, Hispanic students scored 15 points below white students, and Black students scored about 30 points lower than their white peers.
